messages:
Alex: Heads-up — ran a 2h perf sweep on prefix-cache + allocator combos. Seeing repeated small OOM blips when kernel switching happens during short-sequence bursts.
Priya: Can you paste the perf summary? which kernel switch point?
Alex: gist: kernel_selector picks fast-fp16 for <512 tokens, switches to tvm-optimized for >512. When sequence distribution fluctuates, we get transient workspace thrash.
Mateo: That matches the profile I saw yesterday — allocator keeps freeing blocks then immediately reallocating slightly different sizes. high alloc/free rate.
Jin: Do we have flamegraphs? sounds like fragmentation + gap in best-fit behavior.
Alex: Paste of profiler snippet:
```
time    call    size    kernel
0.001   alloc   2.4MB   fast-fp16
0.002   free    2.4MB
0.003   alloc   2.9MB   tvm-opt
0.0035  oom?    -       fallback
```
Lee: OOMs during quick freelist churn — allocator returning to host then cudaMalloc spikes, latency + mem peaks.
Priya: What about batching heuristic? are we mixing large and tiny requests in same batch? that can amplify kernel toggles.
Alex: Yes. current batcher groups by arrival time only. No explicit kernel affinity or seq-len bucketing.
Mateo: Suggestion: prefer batch composition that keeps kernel type homogeneous per batch. small cost to wait 5-10ms to drain short tokens.
Jin: Ok but that hurts P50. maybe make it tiered: if request is latency-sensitive (route header) keep immediate, otherwise soft-wait for 8ms to improve backend efficiency.
Priya: Also prefix-cache shard sizes: many tiny prefixes pinned long TTL -> high KV memory pressure. Could evict cold small prefixes sooner.
Alex: I ran a sim: with TTL=30m vs 6h, hit-rate drops 3% but memory drops 28%. tradeoff looks promising for low-value prefixes.
Lee: What about shard count? we currently keep 128 shards per GPU. increasing shards reduces per-shard eviction granularity but adds metadata overhead.
Mateo: For our workload, smaller shards (256->512) actually improved hit-rate stability because hot keys stayed localized and eviction became more targeted.
Alex: Actionable: add hot-key detection to bump TTL for top 1% keys, TTL fallback for rest.
Priya: Allocator knobs I tested: reducing max_cached_block_count from 64->24 cut fragmentation but increased cudaMalloc calls ~12%. net: latency p95 unchanged, mem tail improved.
Jin: Could we add a workspace pool per kernel variant so switching kernels reuses separate pools instead of freeing to global? that would avoid cross-kernel fragmentation.
Lee: That's pretty good — per-kernel ring buffer for workspace reuse. small overhead to maintain pool, huge wins on churn.
Alex: I prototyped per-kernel pools + kernel-aware batcher. Results: OOMs eliminated in 2/3 stress tests, 18% lower peak mem.
Mateo: Nice. Did you test with simulated long-run churn (24h)? sometimes pools leak if eviction never runs.
Alex: We added TTL on pooled buffers and a periodic sweep. no leaks observed in 24h sim.
Priya: What about fallbacks: when OOM happens, prefer soft-fallback to smaller-quantized model variant instead of failing the request. That keeps availability.
Jin: Agreed. routing policy should try model-quantize fallback first, then region fallback. Avoid expensive recompile in hot paths.
Lee: Also add a perf-bot alert when allocator cudaMalloc rate > X per second for >30s. that correlated strongly with OOM incidents.
perf-bot: ALERT: cudaMalloc spikes detected on node rwd-gpu-08; peak rate 47/s (threshold 15/s). stack: allocator->workspace->kernel-switch.
Alex: Good. Next steps: (1) land kernel-aware batcher + per-kernel workspace pools (PR in progress), (2) experiment with TTL heuristics + hot-key bumping (experiment draft), (3) reduce cached_block_count on allocator as a safety knob, (4) add perf-bot threshold and dashboard.
Priya: Who picks up (2)? I can run the prefix-cache simulation with real traffic traces.
Mateo: I’ll own (1) prototype cleanup and perf run. planning to test A/B on one cluster.
Jin: I can wire the perf-bot alert and dashboard.
Lee: I’ll prepare rollback playbook and a canary for the batcher change.
Alex: Timeline: aim for canary by EOD Fri, full rollout next Tue if stable.
Priya: Quick question — how aggressive should hot-key TTL bumps be? 2x TTL? 10x?
Mateo: Start with 4x TTL for top 1% and monitor hit-rate / mem delta.
Alex: Also note kernel-selector threshold should be smoother — add hysteresis on seq-length decision to avoid flip-flopping around 512. maybe +/- 64 tokens.
Jin: Good idea. jittering threshold can cause pathological oscillation.
perf-bot: SUMMARY: per-kernel pools + kernel-aware batching + TTL tuning + allocator safe defaults. expected outcomes: fewer OOMs, ~15-25% peak mem reduction, stable p95.
Alex: Cool. I'll push the prototype PR and link here.
Priya: Thanks! looping in infra on canary config. :thumbsup:
Mateo: Tagging @Lee for rollback knobs.
Lee: ack
Alex: End of thread — will update with PR link and perf graphs.
